title: POC evaluation sprint kickoff - Shipwright Logistics (model scouting)
summary: Kickoff for a 3-week POC to evaluate open-models for multi-lingual logistics document understanding and routing. Discussed success criteria (accuracy thresholds, latency and cost SLOs), workload sizing (daily/query volumes, peak bursts), candidate models (decoder LLMs vs encoder-decoder hybrids, smaller quantized variants), and benchmarks to run. Agreed timeline, initial test dataset, and next steps to run baseline runs and share security docs.
next_steps: Redwood to share proposed benchmark script + sample dataset link by 2027-05-14
Shipwright to provide 2 weeks of anonymized routing logs and 200 labeled documents by 2027-05-16
Schedule dry-run baseline (hosted) with three models for 2027-05-18
action_items: Ava Martinez: send benchmark harness (GH link) and security one-pager (due 2027-05-14)
Ravi Patel: upload anonymized sample dataset to shared S3 and grant Redwood read access (due 2027-05-16)
Liam O'Connor: prepare initial cost/latency estimates for shortlisted models with quantized options (due 2027-05-17)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-12 14:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood SE), Ravi (Shipwright Head of ML), Maya (Data Platform), Elena (CTO)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Ravi: Hey, Ravi here.
[00:10] Maya: Maya on the call.
[00:12] Elena: Elena here.
[00:15] Liam: Liam, solutions engineering, Redwood.
[00:17] Ava: Great. Quick agenda; align on POC goals, volumes and SLOs, pick an initial model shortlist and agree benchmark plan and timeline.
[00:28] Elena: Sounds good. We're mostly focused on two things: highly accurate multi-lingual extraction from bills of lading and routing heuristics for our hub distribution — so quality and inference latency are both important.
[00:40] Ravi: To add, cost matters — we have seasonal peaks. Need to balance per-token cost with tail latency.
[00:48] Noah: quick clarifying question, when you say multilingual which languages are high priority?
[00:53] Maya: English, Spanish, Portuguese, and Chinese (simplified) — Spanish and Portuguese are about 35% of volume combined.
[01:02] Ava: Good. For the POC scope we propose a 3-week sprint: week 0 baselines and data hygiene, week 1 model runs and latency/cost, week 2 error analysis + decision. Does that align?
[01:15] Elena: Yes, that's the velocity we were hoping for.
[01:19] Liam: On the technical side, we recommend evaluating three model archetypes: a medium-size decoder model (for generation/extraction), an encoder-decoder fine-tuned candidate for structured extraction, and a smaller quantized variant for cost-tier testing. Examples: Llama2-13B variant, an mT5-like encoder-decoder, and a 7B quantized open variant.
[01:41] Ravi: We have an internal fine-tuned BERT pipeline but it struggles with longer documents and multilingual edge cases. Curious how the decoders perform for structured outputs.
[01:51] Ava: We'll include structured prompting/zero-shot templates and also a few few-shot examples. For success criteria, can we agree on thresholds?
[01:58] Maya: For extraction F1 we'd like at least 0.86 on core fields, higher for routing labels (0.9). Latency ideally sub-250ms p95 in production for single document calls, but we're ok with 400-500ms during peak if cost is lower.
[02:14] Liam: That makes sense. We'll run p95 latency measurements and tokenized cost estimates. For the POC we'll run both hosted API runs and a Dedicated capacity simulation to show differences.
[02:27] Ravi: About privacy — some documents have PII. We'll need encryption at rest and audit logs. Do you support KMS integration for private deployments?
[02:36] Ava: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; Redwood Hosted can redact but for PII we suggest a Private or Dedicated environment. We'll attach the security datasheet.
[02:47] Maya: Also need to confirm data residency — EU subset of customers need EU-only processing.
[02:54] Noah: noted. We'll include region routing in the benchmark matrix.
[02:58] Liam: Back to models: trade-offs — decoder models often handle noisy prompts and extraction with flexible templates but can hallucinate if not constrained; encoder-decoder models can be more stable for structured outputs but sometimes need token budgets for long docs.
[03:13] Ravi: For our docs average length is 1.2k tokens, but some go up to 6k. KV cache and long context handling matter.
[03:20] Liam: We'll look at sequence-length profiles and pick model checkpoints that support extended contexts; also consider sliding-window or chunking strategies.
[03:29] Ava: For benchmarking we'll measure: accuracy (F1/precision/recall) on labeled set, latency p50/p95, tokenized cost per call, and robustness across languages. Anything else?
[03:40] Maya: Error typology — false positives on addresses and unit conversion errors — capture that in the eval.
[03:47] Elena: And we'd like to see failure examples annotated so our engineers can triage.
[03:51] Liam: We'll produce an error taxonomy report.
[03:54] Ravi: How do you handle batching? Our throughput is about 120 reqs/min average with 800 reqs/min peak. That will impact cost and latency.
[04:05] Noah: Are those requests single doc synchronous?
[04:07] Ravi: Yes, synchronous calls from our routing pipeline.
[04:10] Liam: We will simulate both continuous burst patterns and steady-state. For Dedicated, batching reduces unit cost but increases tail latency—we'll provide both profiles.
[04:21] Ava: Can you share 2 weeks of trace logs? We'll use that to size GPU pools for Dedicated sims.
[04:28] Maya: Yes, we'll anonymize and upload to S3.
[04:31] Ava: Great. Now model shortlist — proposed initial candidates: 1) Open decoder A (13B) - good generalist with strong few-shot, 2) mT5-large-like encoder-decoder (multilingual), 3) quantized 7B open variant for cost baseline. We'll also include one heavy-duty 70B eval if you want to see top quality tradeoffs.
[04:54] Ravi: I'd like to see the heavy-duty run but limited to a sampled subset because of cost.
[04:59] Liam: makes sense. We'll do 70B on 5% of the set for quality upper bound.
[05:03] Maya: For metrics, please include per-language breakdown and per-field F1.
[05:08] Ava: Will do.
[05:10] Elena: Any thoughts about on-premises? We are exploring private deployment, but initial POC can be in hosted. If the data residency or KMS is blocking, we might need private.
[05:20] Ava: Agreed. We'll run hosted baselines for speed then show Dedicated/Private cost delta. Redwood Private adds platform fees and provisioning time (usually 4-6 weeks), so not part of the 3-week POC; it's an enterprise follow-up.
[05:34] Ravi: That timeline is fine. For the POC decision criteria, what does success look like operationally?
[05:40] Noah: Operational success = meets accuracy thresholds + predictable cost below X per doc + p95 latency under target for at least 80% of traffic profiles.
[05:49] Maya: And maintainable integration with our existing orchestration — minimal SDK changes.
[05:54] Liam: Redwood SDKs already support our routing and batching primitives; we'll provide sample integration code.
[06:00] Ava: Quick question about evaluation harness: do you prefer we run the harness from Redwood infra or give you the harness to run in your environment?
[06:07] Ravi: Prefer you run initial hosted runs and share results, then we'll run gold tests internally to confirm.
[06:13] Liam: Perfect. We'll do an initial smoke run (hosted) on Wednesday and share a report.
[06:18] Maya: On benchmarks, include tokenization counts and breakdown for prompt vs generation tokens.
[06:24] Liam: Will include.
[06:26] Ava: Anything else on constraints? Regulatory or compliance notes?
[06:29] Elena: We'll need an SOC2 attestation and to confirm log retention windows. Also SSO for console access.
[06:36] Ava: We'll attach SOC2 and SSO/SAML docs in the follow-up.
[06:40] Ravi: Back to models — curious about quantization and its effect on multilingual quality. Sometimes quantized models degrade on non-Latin scripts.
[06:50] Liam: Good point, we'll measure per-language deltas and include a quality degradation table for 8-bit/4-bit variants.
[06:58] Ava: Any red team or hallucination tests you'd like added?
[07:02] Elena: Add a hallucination check for instruction-following, and a recall test for PII extraction — avoid false inclusions.
[07:10] Liam: We'll add those to the harness.
[07:13] Ava: Let's recap timeline: Redwood sends harness + security docs by 2027-05-14; Shipwright uploads anonymized dataset by 2027-05-16; dry-run hosted baseline 2027-05-18; full short-list runs 2027-05-20 to 2027-05-22; wrap + decision 2027-06-01.
[07:32] Maya: Works for us.
[07:34] Ravi: One small ask: can you include estimated monthly cost projection for each model at our steady and peak throughput?
[07:41] Liam: yes, we'll produce steady-state and peak monthlyized cost scenarios including Dedicated reserved pricing.
[07:47] Ava: I'll follow up with the pricing sheet and a short mapping of which model archetype maps to Redwood product (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).
[07:55] Elena: Great.
[07:56] Speaker 2: (inaudible)
[07:58] Ava: Any blockers on the data side?
[08:00] Maya: We have to remove certain PII fields before sharing but that's doable in a day or two.
[08:04] Ravi: We'll prioritize the routing logs and sample docs.
[08:07] Ava: Perfect. Last, stakeholders: who should we loop in for the decision?
[08:12] Elena: Myself and Ravi for technical signoff, and our VP of Ops for cost approval (I'll loop them if the numbers look good).
[08:20] Ava: Excellent. We'll also cc our solutions lead for Dedicated if the numbers push that direction.
[08:26] Liam: One more technical note: for long doc handling we'll test chunking with context stitching vs models with extended context, and measure end-to-end latency.
[08:38] Ravi: Good.
[08:40] Ava: OK. Thanks everyone — we'll send the links and docs after this call.
[08:45] Maya: Thanks.
[08:47] Elena: Thank you.
[08:49] Liam: Thanks all.
[08:51] Ava: Meeting adjourned.

[61:50] (call ended)
